senses.gloss:
तृप् 1. तृप्, cl. 4. 5. 6. P. तृप्यति, तृप्-
नोति (Ved. तृप्णोति), तृपति or तृम्पति,
ततर्प; तर्पिष्यति, तर्प्स्यति, त्रप्स्यति; अतृ-
पत्, अतर्पीत्, अतार्प्सीत्, अत्राप्सीत्; तर्प्तुम्, त्रप्-
तुम्, तर्पितुम्; to satisfy one's self, to become
satiated or satisfied, to be pleased or satisfied or con-
tented (with gen., inst., or loc., e. g. नाग्निस् तृप्-
यति काष्ठानाम्, fire is not satisfied with wood;
तृप्यति फलैः, he is satisfied with fruits); to
enjoy; to satisfy, satiate, please; cl. 1. P. तर्पति,
&c., to light up, kindle (i. e. satiate a fire with fuel):
Caus. P. A. तर्पयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अतीतृपत्
and अततर्पत्, to gladden, exhilarate; to satiate,
refresh, satisfy; A. to become satiated or satisfied;
P. to light, kindle: Desid. तितृप्सति, तितर्पिषति,
to wish to satiate one's self, to desire to satisfy:
Desid. of the Caus. तितर्पयिषति, to wish to
satiate or refresh or satisfy: Intens. तरीतृप्यते, त-
रीतर्प्ति and तरीत्रप्ति; [cf. तृम्प्, तृफ्, तृम्फ्:
Gr. τέρτω, τρέφω (?) Old Pruss. en-terpo, ‘to be
useful:’ Lith. tarpstu, ‘to increase, to prosper;’
tarpà, ‘increase:’ Goth. tharf, ‘to satisfy, to be
useful:’ Old Germ. trôstyan: Angl. Sax. thearf:
Hib. tropadh, ‘heavy, grave;’ tromaighim = tar-
payāmi; tormach, ‘increase, augmentation;’ torp,
‘bulk;’ tormad, ‘pregnant, big.’]

2. तृप्, at the end of a comp. in अ-सुतृप् and
पशु-तृप्.
तृपा, f. a kind of plant; [cf. तार्प्य.]

तृपत्, ind., Ved. with pleasure or enjoyment, to
one's satisfaction; (त्), m. a parasol; the moon.

तृपल, अस्, आ, अम् (said by some to be fr. rt.
त्रप्), Ved. quick, restless, hasty, anxious; pleased,
glad; (आ), f. a creeper or creeping plant; [cf.
तृप्र.]
—तृपल-प्रभर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved.
pressing quickly forwards, acting quickly.

तृप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, satiated, satisfied, contented;
(अम्), n. the becoming satiated, satisfaction.
—तृप्-
तांशु (˚त-अं˚), उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having well nou-
rished shoots or members, epithet of the Soma
plant.
—तृप्तात्मन् (˚त-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, having a
contented mind, contented, satisfied, tranquil.

तृप्ताय, nom. A. तृप्तायते, &c., to be or
become satiated or satisfied.

तृप्ति, इस्, f. satisfaction, contentment; satiety,
disgust; hilarity, pleasure, gratification; Ved. water;
[cf. अति-तृप्ति.]
—तृप्ति-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving satis-
faction, pleasing.
—तृप्ति-दीप, अस्, m., N. of a
work.
—तृप्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, satisfied, feeling
satisfaction.
तृप्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, satiated, satisfied.

तृप्र, अस्, आ, अम्, restless, hasty, anxious; pleased,
contented, (compar. त्रपीयस्, superl. त्रपिष्ठ);
(अस्), m. an oblation of ghee or boiled butter.
—तृप्र-दंशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. biting hastily.

तृप्रालु, उस्, उस्, उ, having ghee, but not liking
it or not blending with it.
तृपु तृपु, उस्, m., Ved. a thief; [cf. त्रिपु.]
